speaker: Unknown
en: Hi, and welcome to Grey Matter, the podcast from Greylock.
zh: 大家好，欢迎收听 Greylock 的播客 Grey Matter。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm Sam Motamity, a partner at Greylock.
zh: 我是 Sam Motamity，Greylock 的合伙人。

speaker: Unknown
en: My guest today is Rishabh Jain, who's the CEO and co-founder of Firmat.
zh: 我今天的嘉宾是 Rishabh Jain，他是 Firmat 的 CEO 兼联合创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Firmat provides the tooling and infrastructure to enable distributed e-commerce.
zh: Firmat 提供支持分布式电商的工具和基础设施。

speaker: Unknown
en: Rishabh, thanks for being here today.
zh: Rishabh，感谢你今天来到这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks for having me.
zh: 感谢你们的邀请。

speaker: Unknown
en: Super excited about this conversation.
zh: 我对这次对话非常兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I've been looking forward to it.
zh: 是的，我也一直很期待。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's been a long time, a long time coming.
zh: 已经等了很久了，酝酿了很长时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Rishabh, I want to start, let's rewind the clock back to 2021 when you were beginning to think through and then at the end of the year, start Fermat.
zh: 那么 Rishabh，我想从头说起，让我们把时间拨回 2021 年，当时你开始思考这个问题，然后在年底创立了 Fermat。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the wake of Apple's app tracking transparency rules going into effect.
zh: 那是在 Apple 的应用追踪透明度规则生效之后。

speaker: Unknown
en: Kind of the rise of ATT completely changed how companies think about ads and how they acquire customers.
zh: ATT 的兴起彻底改变了公司对广告以及获取客户方式的思考。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you come from a background before Fermat at LiveRamp really versed in all of this.
zh: 而你在加入 Fermat 之前有着 LiveRamp 的背景，对这一切非常精通。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think Fermat was really born as part of that big transition.
zh: 我认为 Fermat 正是作为那场重大转变的一部分而诞生的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so maybe to start, tell us a little bit about that and how you position Fermat in the new commerce landscape.
zh: 那么作为开始，能跟我们讲讲那段经历，以及你如何在新的商业格局中定位 Fermat 吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, totally.
zh: 好的，当然可以。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's probably helpful to give just 30 seconds on what LiveRamp did, or what LiveRamp does.
zh: 简单用 30 秒介绍一下 LiveRamp 当时做的，或者说 LiveRamp 现在做的事情，应该会有帮助。

speaker: Unknown
en: So LiveRamp provides all of the infrastructure to enable people to track across the open web.
zh: LiveRamp 提供支持人们在开放网络上进行追踪的全部基础设施。

speaker: Unknown
en: So anytime you're trying to find somebody and say that, hey, this is the same person who went to this website, and then this app, and then did this transaction in store, and
zh: 所以任何时候，当你试图找到某个人并确认说，嘿，这就是同一个访问过这个网站，然后又用了这个应用，然后在实体店完成了这笔交易的人，而且

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like a medium-sized public company at this point.
zh: 它现在算是一家中等规模的上市公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was very successful in giving birth to this entire industry that now the entire open ad stack actually takes advantage of.
zh: 它非常成功地催生了整个行业，现在整个开放广告技术栈实际上都在利用这个行业。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that gave me a first-class view into what it means to provide engaging consumer experiences.
zh: 所以这让我得以一流地洞察什么叫做提供有吸引力的消费者体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's the way we thought about it at LiveRamp.
zh: 这就是我们在 LiveRamp 思考问题的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the most engaging consumer experience that you can provide?
zh: 你能提供的最具吸引力的消费者体验是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you can't track people anymore, the entire premise off of which we interact with the consumer internet completely changes.
zh: 而当你再也无法追踪人们的时候，我们与消费者互联网互动的整个前提就彻底改变了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was the core problem statement that I got very excited about.
zh: 这就是让我非常兴奋的那个核心问题陈述。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I remember when you and I first actually, we first met, I was still at Libram, but I was very excited about this problem and I couldn't stop thinking about this problem starting in the summer of 2020.
zh: 我还记得你和我的第一次，我们的第一次见面，当时我还在 Libram，但我对这个问题非常兴奋，从 2020 年夏天开始我就无法停止思考这个这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we met at the end of 2020 and then the company started at the end of 21.
zh: 然后我们在 2020 年底见了面，公司在 21 年底成立。

speaker: Unknown
en: But Fermat's birth was to provide tooling, to provide that infrastructure layer that allows people to provide engaging consumer experiences on the internet in this new world of the internet.
zh: 但 Fermat 的创立是为了提供工具，提供那个基础设施层，让人们能够在这个新的互联网世界中在互联网上提供有吸引力的消费者体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now with other consumer internet changes like AI, I think it is even more obvious that consumer engagement on the consumer internet is going to be completely different than it was in the past.
zh: 现在随着消费者互联网的其他变化，比如 AI，我认为更加显而易见的是，消费者互联网上的消费者参与将与过去完全不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, Rishabh, I was just thinking back to when we met and you started explaining this all to me and I came back to our team, like this is back in early 21 because at Greylock, we've learned to start really large and important companies.
zh: 是的，Rishabh，我刚刚回想起我们见面的时候，你开始向我解释这一切，然后我回到我们团队，那是在 21 年初，因为在 Greylock，我们已经学会了如何创立真正大型且重要的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: There has to be some major shift in the landscape and then you have to insert into that shift and write that shift, whether that's Workday writing the shift to cloud or Figma writing the shift to every company being designer first.
zh: 必须要有格局上的某种重大转变，然后你必须切入那个转变并驾驭那个转变，无论是 Workday 驾驭向云的转变，还是 Figma 驾驭向每家公司以设计师为先的转变。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it felt like you were calling out that, as you just said, the way consumers interact with commerce globally and online was going to dramatically change.
zh: 而我感觉你当时指出的正是，正如你刚才所说，消费者在全球范围内与商业和线上互动的方式将会发生巨大变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think now, three years later, sitting here in April 2024, that's proven to be true and then some.
zh: 而我认为现在，三年后的今天，坐在这里的 2024 年 4 月，这已经被证明是真的，甚至不止如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so maybe just riffing on that for a moment, how have things played out as you expected?
zh: 那么也许就此稍作展开，事情的发展如你所预期的那样吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And also, has anything surprised you in how it's played out around this kind of shifting landscape?
zh: 另外，在这个不断变化的格局中，事情的发展有没有什么让你感到惊讶的地方？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a great question.
zh: 这是个好问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I will share that I am thankful that you came with a beginner's mindset to this industry because I'll tell you that in early 21, when I was first doing discovery, I would call CMOs and ask them like, hey, what are you guys doing about the upcoming Apple changes?
zh: 那么我会说，我很庆幸你是带着初学者心态进入这个行业的，因为我要告诉你，在 21 年初，当我最初做调研的时候，我会打电话给 CMO 们问他们，嘿，你们对即将到来的 Apple 变化在做什么准备？

speaker: Unknown
en: And the first set of answers I got was, what are you talking about?
zh: 我得到的第一批回答是，你在说什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Then the second set of answers I got was, oh yeah, my agency and Facebook says they got it handled.
zh: 然后我得到的第二批回答是，哦是的，我的代理公司和 Facebook 说他们已经搞定了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I could like see in front of my eyes, like, oh my God, nobody believes me.
zh: 所以我可以亲眼看到，哦天哪，没有人相信我。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was this like very typical moment that a lot of founders have, unfortunately, that like, you know, people don't believe you.
zh: 而这是一个非常典型的时刻，很不幸，很多创始人都经历过，就是，你知道，人们不相信你。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then of course, at the beginning of 22,
zh: 然后当然，在 22 年初，

speaker: Unknown
en: The changes actually impacted the industry.
zh: 这些变化确实冲击了这个行业。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'll be candid, I think that the impact was way higher than I expected.
zh: 我会坦白说，我认为冲击比我预期的要大得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so much so that e-commerce businesses went from being money printing machines, which is why seven years ago they were venture funded.
zh: 以至于电商业务从印钞机——这也是七年前它们获得风险投资的原因——

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I knew that it was going to be a high impact, but I did not expect that you would go from contribution margin positive to contribution margin negative.
zh: 我的意思是，我知道冲击会很大，但我没有预料到你会从边际贡献为正变成边际贡献为负。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that changes everything when something like that happens.
zh: 当这样的事情发生时，一切都会改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you saw massive changes in the e-commerce landscape.
zh: 于是你看到了电商格局的巨大变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: The high level is like you saw Facebook stock drop by 80%, you saw Shopify stock drop, e-commerce darlings.
zh: 概括地说，你看到 Facebook 股价下跌了 80%，你看到 Shopify 股价下跌，这些电商宠儿。

speaker: Unknown
en: Got completely revalued.
zh: 被完全重新估值了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The way people thought about funding these businesses completely changed.
zh: 人们对这些业务的融资方式的看法完全改变了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The way people thought about operating these businesses has completely changed.
zh: 人们对这些业务的运营方式的看法完全改变了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So now marketing and finance are closer together than they've ever been.
zh: 所以现在营销和金融比以往任何时候都更紧密地结合在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I would say that while the vector I had predicted was correct, I did not expect the impact to be as significant as it ended up being.
zh: 而我想说，虽然我当初预测的方向是对的，但我没有预料到影响最终会如此巨大。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can tell you from the investor side of the table, we saw that impact.
zh: 我可以从投资人的角度告诉你，我们看到了那种影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: Play out firsthand in a number of commerce businesses that were pitching us and just seeing the unit economics almost overnight, right?
zh: 在一批向我们做融资路演的商务业务中亲身展现出来，就是看到单位经济效益几乎是一夜之间，

speaker: Unknown
en: Just in the process of a couple quarters, like completely flip upside down.
zh: 就在几个季度的时间里，完全翻转了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then to your point, there's both the end businesses and then also the infrastructure layers and the acquisition layers and a Facebook and a Shopify.
zh: 然后正如你所说，既有终端业务，也有基础设施层、获客层，还有 Facebook 和 Shopify。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the answer to that for brands and for people in the commerce ecosystem?
zh: 对于品牌和商务生态系统中的人来说，对此的答案是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Consumers are going to expect experiences that are continuous with the journey that they are on.
zh: 消费者将会期待与他们所处旅程连续一致的体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the backend needs to support closed loop one-to-one experiences.
zh: 而后端需要支持闭环的一对一体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reason this must happen...
zh: 而这件事必须发生的原因是……

speaker: Unknown
en: Is when it is harder to target, you need the journey to be more effective.
zh: 当定向投放变得更难时，你需要旅程更加有效。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that is like the simple thing.
zh: 这就是这么简单的道理。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like it turns out that when I knew Sam was the best next customer for me, I didn't need a perfect journey.
zh: 就像，事实证明，当我确定 Sam 是我的最佳下一位客户时，我并不需要一个完美的旅程。

speaker: Unknown
en: I could do with a bad journey because Sam was so predisposed to buying my product and I could just go fishing and find Sam and bring him to my website.
zh: 我可以接受一个糟糕的旅程，因为 Sam 是那么倾向于购买我的产品，我只需要去“钓鱼”找到 Sam，把他带到我的网站。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's no longer true.
zh: 这已不再成立。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you need a great journey.
zh: 所以你需要一个出色的旅程。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the second thing is you need it to be closed loop.
zh: 然后第二件事是你需要它是闭环的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, and this closed loop idea is one that is completely underappreciated.
zh: 所以，这个闭环的概念是一个被完全低估的概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'll share some of the ways this has played out in the ecosystem.
zh: 我会分享一些这在生态系统中已经展现出来的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the reason you need it to be closed loop now is when you can no longer track people, you need for the transaction event to be directly correlated to the intention event.
zh: 你现在需要它是闭环的原因是，当你再也无法追踪用户时，你需要交易事件与意图事件直接相关联。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Facebook has done this by doing Facebook shops.
zh: Facebook 通过做 Facebook shops 实现了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: TikTok has done this by doing TikTok shops.
zh: TikTok 通过做 TikTok shops 实现了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have also done this by partnering Amazon and Facebook, where you can now do an Amazon transaction inside of Facebook.
zh: 他们还通过与 Amazon 和 Facebook 合作实现了这一点，现在你可以在 Facebook 内部完成一笔 Amazon 交易。

speaker: Unknown
en: Three years ago, that would have never happened.
zh: 三年前，那是绝不会发生的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You would have never seen Facebook giving control of their feed to Amazon.
zh: 你绝不会看到 Facebook 把他们信息流的控制权交给 Amazon。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is a crazy change to the consumer internet that is totally underappreciated.
zh: 那是消费互联网上一个疯狂的变化，却被完全低估了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It has also led to the rise of retail media networks.
zh: 这也导致了零售媒体网络的兴起。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you're seeing a very large set of companies, Instacart, Uber, all of these companies, you can see their revenue go up very meaningfully on the retail media side.
zh: 所以你看到一大批公司，Instacart、Uber，所有这些公司，你可以看到它们在零售媒体方面的收入有非常显著的上涨。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there are companies like us.
zh: 然后还有像我们这样的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who we are fortunate to be creating this category where you can actually have a unique site experience for every piece of content that you deploy.
zh: 我们很幸运能够创建这个品类，让你可以真正为部署的每一条内容都拥有一个独特的站点体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: So now the brand can actually own that consumer journey while still deploying it one-to-one to every piece of content.
zh: 所以现在品牌可以真正拥有那条消费者旅程，同时仍然将一对一的部署应用到每一条内容上。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're very lucky that that has led to very, very fast growth and adoption because the need for these types of tools is so severe.
zh: 我们非常幸运，这带来了非常非常快的增长和采用，因为对这类工具的需求是如此迫切。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you're just seeing the pull happen in every element, whether it's Facebook shops, retail media networks, or us.
zh: 而且你会看到这种拉动在每个环节都在发生，无论是 Facebook shops、零售媒体网络，还是我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just, it has to happen.
zh: 它就是，必须发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, yeah.
zh: 对，对。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, just as you were talking about kind of the pool, I'm reflecting on, uh, Fremont board meetings were always a joy because I come in and the message is always the same, which is we thought we'd have a great quarter and we had an even better quarter than we thought, which I think part of that is credit to you and the team, but part of it is also, I think, a statement on what's happening in the underlying market and just the importance of this new tooling and infrastructure for these customers.
zh: 而且，你知道，就在你谈到那种拉动的时候，我在回顾，呃，Fremont 的董事会会议总是一件乐事，因为我走进来，传达的信息总是一样的，就是我们本来以为会有一个很棒的季度，结果我们的季度比想的还要好，我想这部分功劳归于你和团队，但另一部分也是对底层市场正在发生的事情的一个说明，以及对这些客户来说这套新工具和基础设施的重要性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so maybe like, Rishabh, are there one or two specific stories you could share
zh: 那么，也许，Rishabh，你能不能分享一两个具体的故事

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I'm absolutely happy to.
zh: 是的，我非常乐意。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I would share two specific examples.
zh: 那么我会分享两个具体的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first is a customer in the health and wellness space called MindBodyGreen.
zh: 第一个是健康保健领域的一家客户，叫 MindBodyGreen。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I remember there was a Monday at like 10 a.m.
zh: 我记得那是一个周一，大概上午 10 点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just started to see like new store creation notifications at a very high rate and something like 60 different stores were created in the course of an hour or so.
zh: 我开始以非常高的频率看到新商店创建的通知，大约一小时左右的时间里创建了差不多 60 家不同的商店。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was like, what is going on here?
zh: 我当时就想，这里发生了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was one of those moments where you saw the customer doing something that you knew at some point would happen, but it happened at a rate and in a way in which I could not have predicted.
zh: 那是你看到客户在做某件事的时刻之一，你知道这件事迟早会发生，但它发生的速度和方式是我无法预测的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I learned later
zh: 于是我后来了解到

speaker: Unknown
en: That what they were starting to do was think about customer acquisition, not just as like what ad and what creative drives a customer to do something, but actually it's like a full funnel.
zh: 他们开始做的事情是把客户获取，不只是当作什么广告、什么创意素材驱动客户去做某事，而是把它当作一个完整的漏斗。

speaker: Unknown
en: So like, what is the journey I want to put somebody on that leads to what business outcome for me?
zh: 那么，我想把用户带入怎样的旅程，才能为我带来商业成果？

speaker: Unknown
en: And they started to use that data.
zh: 然后他们开始使用这些数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: They then piped that data to the backend and they do a bunch of analytics to think about things like not only what is the best way to acquire, but also how do you think about what types of SKUs to push out?
zh: 他们接着把这些数据传到后端，做大量分析，思考的问题不仅是最佳获客方式，还包括如何决定推出哪些类型的 SKU。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you sell those SKUs?
zh: 如何销售这些 SKU？

speaker: Unknown
en: What types of SKUs should go as single purchases versus repeat purchase and things like that?
zh: 哪些类型的 SKU 适合单次购买，哪些适合复购，诸如此类？

speaker: Unknown
en: And that type of thinking was exceptional.
zh: 这种思维方式非常出色。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it showed me that you can actually not only
zh: 它让我看到，你实际上不仅可以

speaker: Unknown
en: Reattain strong acquisition, but you can actually start to drive your business in this new mode of thinking.
zh: 重新获得强劲的获客能力，还可以开始用这种新的思维模式来驱动业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's one.
zh: 这是第一个故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other story that I can share is True Classic is a very large Ben's shirt retailer, basically, online.
zh: 我可以分享的另一个故事是，True Classic 基本上是一个规模非常大的在线男装衬衫零售商。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we are starting to see ourselves get pulled into use cases that we truly did not expect.
zh: 而我们开始发现，自己被卷入了一些我们完全没有预料到的使用场景。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I'll hint at some of the types of things that we are starting to get pulled into.
zh: 我先透露一下我们开始被卷入的一些使用类型。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for example, some of our experiences with them don't even have a transaction.
zh: 比如说，我们与某些客户的体验中甚至根本没有交易。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have other engagement goals.
zh: 他们有其他参与目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when you start to see yourself getting used in these new ways by these like
zh: 所以当你开始发现自己正以这些新方式被使用时，被那些

speaker: Unknown
en: Highly engaged customers who are at the cutting edge.
zh: 处于最前沿、高度参与的客户使用时。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's when you can see that like, hey, this thesis of the way that the consumer interacts with the internet or the consumer internet will change.
zh: 这时你才能看到，嘿，消费者与互联网或消费互联网交互的方式将会改变，这个论点是成立的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And here's why, right?
zh: 原因如下，对吧？

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

zh: 所以我认为在商业旅程中会发生两件事，我们正在实践中看到它上演。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: created that surprise and delight moment.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: Or the second thing they're trying to do is have the highest possible average order value for somebody who may already know about them, who wants to try a bunch of their products.
zh: 或者他们想做的第二件事，是让那些可能已经了解他们、想尝试他们多款产品的人，拥有尽可能高的平均订单价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so an example of something that happens when you interact with them through us is you see somebody wearing like, you know, the traditional T-shirt.

en: That doesn't exist.

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the beautiful thing, if I'm kind of understanding it correctly, is you measure the efficacy of that in increased conversion, increased transaction size, and fundamentally of stronger business.

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's also a use case of AI that directly connects to the KPIs that the business cares about.

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly.

speaker: Unknown
en: And to expect any different at this moment when people are talking about how generative AI is going to replace...

speaker: Unknown
en: The way that you know this is inevitable is that people prefer to ask Perplexity or ChatGPT or name your favorite AI tool a question because they can then ask the questions in the format that they want to in order to get the information in the format that they want it.

speaker: Unknown
en: That is for text.
zh: 那是针对文本的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what is the obvious end state of that for commerce?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's what we're talking about.

speaker: Unknown
en: It's obvious and it is already happening.

speaker: Unknown

zh: 那么你们在这个平台中叠加了这种 AI 能力和这种基于 AI 的个性化之后，这对 Fermat 的业务产生了什么影响？

speaker: Unknown
en: The best thing about our business is we actually talk very little about AI to our customers.
zh: 我们业务最好的一点是，我们实际上很少向客户谈论 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is just, you know, something I believe in general about technology is like...

speaker: Unknown
en: Any good technology is indiscernible from magic, but also the customer or consumer doesn't care.
zh: 任何好的技术都难以与魔法区分，但同样，客户或消费者也不在乎。

speaker: Unknown
en: They need their problem solved.
zh: 他们需要的是他们的问题被解决。

speaker: Unknown
en: It turns out that people just want their problem solved, and how they get their problem solved is irrelevant to them.
zh: 事实证明，人们只是想让他们的问题被解决，至于问题是怎么被解决的，对他们来说无关紧要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the problem that we solve for our customers is this sort of idea that you can create a different experience for every journey that you are launching.

speaker: Unknown
en: And we have solved that problem, and we set up ambitious goals for this year.

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm surprised by the rate of growth, even given those ambitious goals that we have set.
zh: 即便考虑到我们设定的那些雄心勃勃的目标，增长速度仍然让我感到惊讶。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we're seeing adoption that is very, very fast.
zh: 所以我们看到 adoption 的速度非常、非常快。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are seeing growth in actual usage on the platform that is very, very fast.
zh: 我们看到平台上的实际使用量增长得非常、非常快。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if I'm being totally candid, it's like...

speaker: Unknown
en: That level of growth, when it happens that quickly, you then encounter a totally different set of problems, which is now the set of problems we have the fortune to be able to solve.

speaker: Unknown
en: But you get this feeling that it's like, okay, wow, we are really able to help these businesses.

speaker: Unknown
en: We can meaningfully move metrics in a way in which people are very thankful and publicly thankful about how the impact is being felt.

speaker: Unknown
en: Which then drives other customers that we get the benefit of being able to help, which drives the best employees in the industry to want to join you.

speaker: Unknown
en: The net of it for me is...

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that when you are creating a platform that will help change how people interact with the consumer internet, you want to do the maximum amount of net positive good for everybody who interacts with you.
zh: 我认为，当你在创建一个将帮助改变人们与消费者互联网互动方式的平台时，你会想要为每一个与你互动的人创造最大程度的净正面价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we are doing that for our customers.
zh: 所以我们正在为我们的客户这样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are doing that for our employees.
zh: 我们正在为我们的员工这样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And of course, I hope we do that for our shareholders, right?
zh: 当然，我也希望我们为我们的股东这样做，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's sort of like how I am currently thinking about it, given the opportunity that we have.
zh: 考虑到我们所拥有的机会，这就是我目前对此的思考方式。

en: One of the things you said right now that really resonated with me is like, at the end of the day, the customer doesn't care about AI, generative AI.
zh: 你刚才说的一件事真的引起了我的共鸣，那就是：归根结底，客户不在乎 AI，不在乎生成式 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: The customer cares about their business problem.
zh: 客户在乎的是他们的业务问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you can use generative AI or AI to kind of solve that business problem, fantastic.
zh: 如果你能用生成式 AI 或 AI 来解决那个业务问题，那太好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you have to have clarity that what the customer cares about is the business problem.
zh: 但你必须清楚地认识到，客户在乎的是业务问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: How have you navigated that?
zh: 你是怎么应对这一点的？

en: I mean, Richav, as you know, most founders building companies today, they're either AI-enabled or they're AI-native, right?

speaker: Unknown
en: And if they're not, they should really be asking why they're not.
zh: 而如果他们不是，他们真的应该问问自己为什么不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then I think there's a question of like, okay, how much do I lean into that in my customer positioning?

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: So in general, I take the view that it is very important that when you say what your problem statement is, that you have people nodding along and people meaning your customers.
zh: 所以总体上，我的观点是：当你陈述你的问题定义时，非常重要的一点是要让人们点头认同——所谓人们，指的是你的客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're just like, yeah, that is such a pain.
zh: 他们就是那种反应：对，这真是个痛点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, you know, and the problem statement I say is like, man, CAC on Facebook is totally ridiculous.
zh: 比如，你知道，我说的问题定义就是：天哪，Facebook 上的 CAC 简直离谱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's like, that's easy to nod along to.
zh: 所以，这种说法很容易让人点头认同。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then after that, you have to like convince them why your approach to solving that problem is actually like a good approach, which is a separate thing.
zh: 然后在那之后，你必须说服他们，为什么你解决这个问题的方法确实是一个好方法，这是另一回事。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you want people nodding along to the problem.
zh: 但你要让人们对问题本身点头认同。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I don't think that people nod along to like...
zh: 而我认为人们不会对这样的说法点头认同……

speaker: Unknown
en: Hey, what is the right way to use AI for X?
zh: 嘿，针对 X,使用 AI 的正确方式是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think what that does is that raises questions.
zh: 我认为那样做只会引发疑问。

speaker: Unknown
en: It does not lead to people nodding along.
zh: 它不会让人们点头认同。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so positioning to me is more about first, how do you get people to nod along?
zh: 所以对我来说，定位首先是，你如何让人们点头认同？

speaker: Unknown
en: Then it's about how do you get people to know you like you, trust you, and then they will buy your solution, right?
zh: 然后是，你如何让人们认识你、喜欢你、信任你，然后他们就会购买你的解决方案，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when I think about company building, now I think it is...
zh: 所以当我思考公司建设时，现在我认为……

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a bad idea to not use the best possible tools to solve that person's problem.
zh: 不使用最好的工具去解决那个人的问题，是一个坏主意。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's why I think it's very important.
zh: 所以这就是为什么我认为这非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, to choose to not be AI-enabled or AI-native I think is not a great idea because somebody else could build your business and choose to take that route and then they are using the best possible tools to build that business.
zh: 我是说，我认为选择不做 AI 赋能或 AI 原生的公司不是一个好主意，因为别人可以创建和你一样的业务，选择走那条路，然后他们就是在用最好的工具来构建那个业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's actually the core issue from my standpoint.
zh: 而这其实在我看来就是核心问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, exactly.
zh: 是的,没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that connects to the question you were posing to me, which is like, the key thing is to have clarity on what's the customer problem and how you're going to solve and whether or not you're truly solving it.
zh: 我认为这和你之前向我提出的问题相呼应,也就是,关键在于清楚客户的痛点是什么、你打算怎么解决,以及你是否真正在解决它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And everything else
zh: 而其余的一切

speaker: Unknown
en: Can be iterated on.
zh: 都可以迭代。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reason why I say if you're not AI-enabled or AI-native, you should really reconsider, it's not because that's the North Star.
zh: 我之所以说,如果你没有实现 AI 化或者不是 AI 原生的,你就真的应该重新考虑,并不是因为那是北极星。

speaker: Unknown
en: The North Star is solving the customer problem.
zh: 北极星是解决客户的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's more an empirical observation that the underlying technology has gotten so strong, both from a generative perspective and a predictive perspective.
zh: 这更多是一种经验性的观察:底层技术已经变得非常强大,无论是从生成式角度还是预测式角度。

speaker: Unknown
en: That I think it's highly unlikely there aren't ways to kind of 10X your customer value by leaning into it.
zh: 以至于我认为,如果你不深入拥抱它,却想要 10 倍提升客户价值,这种可能性是极低的——也就是说,拥抱它才很可能找到 10 倍提升客户价值的途径。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, Rishabh, to your point, if you don't, then you leave kind of the door open for someone else to come.
zh: 所以,Rishabh,正如你所说,如果你不这么做,那就等于给别人留了进门的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, I think Fermat's like an exceptional example of that just from my vantage point, which is, you know, again, if I rewind to when we partnered together in 21,
zh: 再说一次,我认为 Fermat 从我的视角来看就是一个格外突出的例子,你知道,再回溯到我们 21 年合作的时候,

speaker: Unknown
en: For us, it was like, hey, here's a founder who understands this domain really well and kind of sees ahead and can see ahead of the next corner and is exceptional in that way.
zh: 对我们来说,当时是:嘿,这里有一位对这个领域理解非常深的创始人,能够预见下一个拐角,并且在这方面格外出色。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then here's a really big shift happening to kind of the interaction between consumers and the internet.
zh: 然后当时正在发生一场很大的转变,关乎消费者与互联网之间的交互方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And candidly, AI was not part of the investment thesis.
zh: 坦白说,AI 并不在当时的投资论点之内。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I, you know, commend you and the team, which is like, okay, you're in these customer accounts, you're learning, there's a fast feedback loop.
zh: 但我,你知道,赞赏你和团队,就是:好吧,你们在客户的账户里,你们在学习,有一个快速的反馈循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it's, you know, going back to what you said earlier, which is how do we keep making these consumer journeys more effective?
zh: 然后就是,你知道,回到你之前说的:我们如何持续让这些消费者旅程更有效?

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, well, there's a way we can drive radical personalization in a way the industry's never seen that I see in the data is leading to kind of performance and ROAS and characteristics on customers that, you know, are unheard of.
zh: 哦,有一种方式可以推动行业前所未见的极致个性化,而且我从数据中看到,这正在带来绩效、ROAS 以及客户特征上,你知道,前所未有的表现。

speaker: Unknown
en: By leveraging AI.
zh: 通过利用 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we didn't start as an AI company, per se.
zh: 所以严格来说,我们并不是作为一家 AI 公司起步的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We started, and still are, a company focused on building the next generation of commerce.
zh: 我们当时起步、现在依然是,一家专注于构建下一代商务的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: It turns out that we're leveraging AI to enable that, and that's led to a dramatic acceleration in the business and enhancement of the impact.
zh: 结果是我们在利用 AI 来实现这一点,而这给业务带来了急剧的加速,也放大了影响力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like that is just such a perfect example to me of what it means to have clarity around the customer problem, but an innovative DNA that enables you to kind of co-opt the latest and greatest from a technology perspective to kind of solve that customer problem.
zh: 对我来说,这就是一个完美的例子,说明既要对客户问题有清晰认知,又要有创新 DNA,让你能够吸纳技术上最新最好的东西,来解决那个客户问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I totally agree.
zh: 是的,我完全同意。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the reasons why it's useful to ask yourself, like, hey, what is the way that you're leveraging AI, is you have no choice but to ask, how do you leverage AI that is going to be AI four years from now or six years from now, not the AI today?
zh: 之所以要问自己“嘿,你利用 AI 的方式是什么”是有用的,其中一个原因是:你别无选择,只能去问,你如何利用那种四年或六年之后的 AI,而不是今天的 AI?

speaker: Unknown
en: Because you have to, you're building a business for the long term.
zh: 因为你必须这样,你是在为长期构建一门生意。

speaker: Unknown
en: The only way you can actually build compounding value is if in your system there is something that gives you a compounding advantage that future AI tools can continue to take advantage of.
zh: 你真正能构建复利价值的唯一方式,是你的系统里存在某种能给你带来复利优势的东西,让未来的 AI 工具能够持续加以利用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then those businesses will actually accelerate even faster because the tools of the future are going to take advantage of those compounding benefits in an even bigger way.
zh: 这样那些企业会加速得更快,因为未来的工具会以更大的方式利用那些复利优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: The reason I like the litmus test of how do you use AI is because it forces the question of what is that underlying compounding advantage that other people are not going to be able to catch up to that will continue to allow tools like AI to drive leverage on your compounding advantage.
zh: 我喜欢“你如何使用 AI”这个试金石的原因在于,它逼出了这样一个问题:那个别人无法追赶的底层复利优势是什么,它将持续让 AI 这样的工具在你的复利优势上发挥杠杆作用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I completely agree.
zh: 是的,我完全同意。

speaker: Unknown
en: And just to add and build on that, I think it is...
zh: 再补充和延伸一下,我认为这是……

speaker: Unknown
en: Being in the customer workflow in a way where your product is tied to a metric or some form of ROI that AI can directly drive, and then also have kind of the data loop where you're building a data set that kind of compounds and enables you to get better and better.
zh: 以一种你的产品与某个指标或某种 ROI 挂钩的方式嵌入客户工作流,并且 AI 能够直接驱动该指标,同时还拥有数据循环,让你构建一个能够复利、让你越做越好的数据集。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, Rishabh, maybe speaking about kind of the future and AI continuing to get better, maybe as a closing question, I'd ask, like, help us dream about the future.
zh: 那么,Rishabh,也许聊聊未来和 AI 持续变好这个话题,作为收尾问题,我想问,帮我们畅想一下未来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And like, you know, two years from now, three years from now, five years from now, what's going to be possible with AI in commerce and in the way consumers sort of interact with the internet?
zh: 比如,你知道,两年后、三年后、五年后,AI 在商务领域以及消费者与互联网交互方式上,将会有什么成为可能?

speaker: Unknown
en: And how are you thinking about kind of realizing that possibility through for a month?
zh: 以及你如何思考通过 for a month 去实现那种可能性?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so...
zh: 是的,那么……

speaker: Unknown
en: I saw on TwitterRx a week or so ago a very well-known technologist.
zh: 大约一周前,我在 TwitterRx 上看到一位非常有名的技术专家。

speaker: Unknown
en: He created this demo, which was essentially interacting with a chatbot that felt sort of like you were interacting with Wirecutter, but it was personalized to you.
zh: 他做了一个演示,本质上是在和一个聊天机器人交互,感觉有点像你在和 Wirecutter 交互,但它是为你个性化的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So basically it was like, hey, what is the best stroller recommendation for me?
zh: 基本上就是:嘿,对我而言最好的婴儿车推荐是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it would ask you questions
zh: 然后它会问你问题

speaker: Unknown
en: to get to know you better because it knows the attributes of a stroller that are relevant to then provide the best possible recommendations.
zh: 来更好地了解你,因为它知道婴儿车的哪些属性是相关的,从而给出尽可能好的推荐。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it gave you recommendations based on that.
zh: 然后它基于这些给了你推荐。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'll tell you that the recommendations it gave me on the stroller question were very good.
zh: 我告诉你,它就婴儿车问题给我的推荐非常好。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the same recommendations that I would give.
zh: 和我自己会给出的推荐一模一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reason I chose strollers is, as you know, I'm a parent and I'm...
zh: 而我之所以选婴儿车,是因为你知道,我是位家长,而且我……

speaker: Unknown
en: Like did an incredible amount of research on strollers when we were having our kid.
zh: 在我们要孩子的时候,对婴儿车做了大量研究。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I consider myself like a stroller connoisseur.
zh: 所以我认为自己算是个婴儿车行家。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was like, wow, this thing gave the same recommendations I would give.
zh: 我当时就想:哇,这东西给出的推荐和我自己会给的一模一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's incredible.
zh: 这太不可思议了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that level of like feeling like I am interacting with a service or whatever it is that understands what I am here for and what my circumstances.
zh: 而且那种感觉——就像我在与一个服务或 whatever 的东西交互,它理解我来这里是干什么、我的处境是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And therefore providing me with the best possible solution to the sets of things that I'm trying to solve for right now is how every consumer experience is going to feel like.
zh: 并因此为我提供针对我当下要解决的问题集的最佳可能方案——这就是每一个消费者体验将会有的感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you can take it from as naive as
zh: 比如你可以从一个很天真的例子说起

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, a lot of consumers will have this like, man, I hate this like free shipping threshold.
zh: 你知道,很多消费者都会有这种想法:天哪,我讨厌这个免运费门槛。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I have to buy something to make the free shipping.
zh: 就是我得再买点东西才能凑够免运费。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you can take it from as simple as that, where you can actually start to manage against that type of objection or just fill that for the person.
zh: 你可以从这么简单的例子开始,你其实可以开始针对那类异议进行管理,或者直接替那个人把它填上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just saying like, hey, I know you're irritated by this free shipping threshold.
zh: 直接说:嘿,我知道你对这个免运费门槛很恼火。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's like the way to get just over it, right?
zh: 这里有个刚好能超过它的办法,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's like doing it for you, for the things that you are expecting that person to want to actually seek in that experience, that's how commerce is going to feel, which today is like totally unimaginable because we take so many things for granted.
zh: 就是在那个体验里,替那个人做你预期他真正想去找的事情,这就是商务将会有的感觉,而这在今天完全是不可想象的,因为我们把太多事情当成理所当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like we take for granted that like, hey, when I go into this thing, I'm going to have to like pick it out of all of these SKUs.
zh: 比如我们理所当然地认为:嘿,当我进入这个东西时,我得从所有这些 SKU 里把它挑出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think none of that is going to happen anymore.
zh: 我认为这些都不会再发生了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you're really going to have an experience that feels catered to the circumstance that you are in that moment in time.
zh: 你真正会拥有的,是一种感觉像是为你当时所处的那种境况量身定制的体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that the reason that that's necessary is not only because people will, again, get trained on that behavior because they're interacting with chatbots and Gen.AI in general,
zh: 而且我认为之所以这是必要的,不仅因为人们会再次被训练出那种行为,因为他们在和聊天机器人以及整个生成式 AI 交互,

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think it's also necessary because that's the only way that you're going to build a sustainable econ business because the idea that you're going to be able to track people is just getting less and less likely.
zh: 但我认为它也是必要的,因为这是你构建一个可持续的 econ 业务的唯一途径,因为那种你还能够追踪人的想法正变得越来越不可能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's like out of both the necessity and out of consumer expectation, we can kind of see the landscape quite clearly emerging in this way.
zh: 所以,出于必要性和消费者期望这两方面,我们已经可以相当清晰地看到这种格局正在以这种方式浮现。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, that's a great articulation and an exciting future for us to all look forward to.
zh: 是的,这是一个很棒的阐述,也是一个我们所有人都可以期待的激动人心的未来。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm excited to see the role that Fermat plays in pioneering that future for our customers and for commerce and consumer internet relationships more broadly.
zh: 我很期待看到 Fermat 在为我们的客户、为整个商务和更广泛的消费者互联网关系开创那个未来中所扮演的角色。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Rishabh, thanks for joining us and sharing a little bit more about that.
zh: 所以 Rishabh,感谢你加入我们并分享更多这方面的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, Sam, thank you for having me.
zh: 是的,Sam,感谢你的邀请。

speaker: Unknown
en: This was really fun.
zh: 这次真的很有趣。
